extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of philosophy, history of science, and readers of Bacon's Novum Organum
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria for judging the intrinsic and historical value of Francis Bacon's logical/philosophical works (Novum Organum, Sylva Sylvarum, De Augmentis, etc.), including their pedagogical effect, doctrinal permanence, method, examples, style, and influence on science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational/stimulating value to young readers
rubrics_metrics.description: The work's ability to 'guard, stimulate, and discipline the intellect' and to bring young students 'into contact with works of real genius' (First Book of the Novum Organum is singled out).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for features that foster habits of cautious and independent investigation, memorable maxims (quoted examples given), striking diction and illustrations that lodge in memory and influence thought. Anti-patterns: dry manuals lacking stimulus; works that fail to connect with students' minds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit epistemic duties communicated
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the work clearly teaches duties such as 'taking nothing upon trust which we can verify for ourselves; rigidly examining our first principles; being on our guard against delusions ... forming our conclusions slowly ... constantly checking them by comparison with the facts of nature and life; avoiding merely subtle and frivolous disputations; confining our enquiries to questions of which the solution is within our power; subordinating all our investigations to the welfare of man and society.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate presence, clarity, and forcefulness of these exhortations. High value if they are stated in forcible/pointed language that can influence generations. Anti-pattern: exhortations stated only rhetorically without concrete methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amount of definite logical doctrine of permanent value
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of 'the amount of definite logical doctrine, comprised in them, which retains any permanent value' (i.e., which of Bacon's individual precepts remain useful now).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish general maxims from specific technical prescriptions; note authorial warning that critics often dismiss almost all precepts — evaluate case-by-case. Scoring should consider endurance and applicability of doctrines to modern logic/science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of deductive reasoning (syllogism) versus induction
rubrics_metrics.description: How Bacon regards the syllogism (deduction) relative to induction — accused of underrating deduction but assigning it 'a co-ordinate rank' when used to apply truths arrived at by induction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the work: (a) correctly balances deduction and induction; (b) recognizes when deduction is valuable for praxis; (c) mischaracterizes one side. Examples/quotations (Bacon's 'Deductio ad Praxin') may be used as evidence. Penalize overstatement that dismisses one mode entirely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment and regulation of hypothesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the text gives adequate rules for legitimate employment of hypothesis — criticism: Bacon 'detracted ... by depreciating hypothesis and neglecting to lay down rules for its legitimate employment', though he admitted 'Permissio Intellectus' in some passages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate explicitness and usefulness of guidance on forming and testing hypotheses. Positive mark if the work reconciles inductive data collection with responsible hypothesis formation; negative if it forbids hypothesis or fails to constrain its misuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of gradual ascent from particulars to axioms/generalisation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Baconian method of 'gradual ascent from particular facts, through axioms of successive degrees of generality, up to the highest generalisations' and whether this is an effective method for representing laws of nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess (a) whether method is well-explained and (b) whether it historically or practically contributed to scientific progress (example: steps leading to theory of Gravitation argued to follow this order). Note that method may be convenient for representing laws once established but not necessarily how investigators actually work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value and precision of the 'Tables' (canons of induction)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tables at the beginning of the Second Book are 'rude and imperfect anticipations' of later 'Canons of Induction' and are made more vague by use of the term 'Form' instead of clearer terms like Law/Cause/Conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate completeness, precision, and terminological clarity of any enumerated canons/tables. Penalize vagueness (terminology like 'Form'); reward anticipatory structural ideas that prefigure later rigorous canons (Herschel, Mill).

rubrics_metrics.name: Praerogativae Instantiarum: conceptual utility and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Bacon's 'Praerogativae Instantiarum' still furnish apt logical terminology and precisely describe types of reasoning; caveat that the scientific examples are often 'wrongly stated, trivial, or inappropriate.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the conceptual clarity and terminological durability of these instances; evaluate the quality and appropriateness of scientific examples — penalize numerous trivial or incorrect examples; reward apt terminology that survives into modern usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation of Observation to Experiment and to Induction
rubrics_metrics.description: The work's conception and statement of how Observation relates to Experiment and how both relate to the rational process of Induction — described here as 'well conceived and stated by Bacon.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for a clear account distinguishing observational reporting, experimental manipulation, and inferential induction. High marks for clarity and usefulness in methodological instruction; low marks if conflated or ill-defined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctrine of fallacies ('Idola') and their pedagogical prominence
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion, clarity, and treatment of the doctrine of Fallacies ('Idola') as an aid to understanding sources of error (idola tribus, specus, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether fallacies are identified, exemplified, and linked to corrective methodological advice. Reward systematic lists with concrete examples and mitigation strategies; penalize mere allusion without operational guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and precision of terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of clear technical terms (Law, Cause, Conditions) versus vague or archaic terms (e.g., use of 'Form') which render reasoning 'more or less vague and obscure.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the author's choice of terms and whether they aid precise argumentation. Penalize archaic/ambiguous vocabulary that obscures reasoning; reward precise contemporary equivalents or clear definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and appropriateness of scientific examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the scientific examples used to illustrate points are accurate, non-trivial, and appropriate (criticized here as 'far too numerous' and frequently 'wrongly stated, trivial, or inappropriate').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score examples on correctness, illustrative power, and relevance. Subtract for erroneous or misleading examples even if rhetorically engaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and historical priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims about whether Bacon 'originated' the reformation of science or simply reflected and popularised an existing movement — criticisms that the reformation was 'the gradual product of the age' and not the work of a single man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate evidence for originality: unique methods, formulations, or decisive influence on later practitioners. Distinguish rhetorical priority from substantive methodological innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete scientific contributions and influence on practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Bacon's method and writings provided direct, practical assistance to scientists (critics claim he 'contributed nothing to science himself' or that Newton/Galileo derived little), versus providing a general road-map or inspiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine historical cases (Newton, Galileo, others) for direct methodological adoption or influence. Reward clear lines of influence and practical uptake; penalize attribution of influence based solely on national pride or rhetorical praise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorial style, diction, and rhetorical power
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of Bacon's diction and style: 'quaintness of expression', 'power of illustration', memorable maxims versus criticisms of stiffness, lack of elegance in Latin/English, and 'stiff and rigid' style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether style aids pedagogical and rhetorical power (memorable maxims, images) or hinders clarity (stiffness, far-fetched similes). Note that striking diction can compensate for technical shortcomings when fostering intellectual habits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for modern students familiar with later treatises
rubrics_metrics.description: Parts of Bacon's work (e.g., the Tables) may be of 'not much intrinsic value to a student who is already familiar with recent treatises.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the work's added value for readers at different levels: introductory pedagogical usefulness versus redundancy for students already versed in later, more refined formulations. Score utility conditional on reader's background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophical/theological implications and controversies (final causes, atheism)
rubrics_metrics.description: How Bacon's questioning of Final Causes and other positions interacts with theological interpretation (accusations of atheism by critics), and whether such questioning legitimately amounts to atheism or is misread.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the nuance with which the work treats teleology and whether critics' theological judgments are fair. Distinguish methodological naturalism from metaphysical atheism; penalize rhetoric that confuses methodological critique with denial of religious sentiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorial credibility and motives (charges of charlatanism or imposture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Critical claims about Bacon's character and motives — e.g., being a 'pretender to philosophy', 'charlatan', or 'conscious that in most instances he is not truthful' — which bear on trust in his method and claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat claims about motive with historical caution: evaluate on evidence rather than invective. Substantive methodological failures are weightier than ad hominem accusations; penalize reliance on character attacks rather than documented methodological problems.
